title: Why this sphere exists
summary: An LLM wired into a larger system is a component with a boundary. Each incident in this sphere is about the boundary being overstepped: live model seats receiving hidden or psychic material they were not entitled to see, a helper inventing an operational fact or entitlement rather than admitting it is unknown, an observer being able to mutate the thing it observes, or a capability silently substituted when a credential is absent. They are real, repeated failures in this project's own agent- and assistant-integration work.
evidence_note: Grounding lives in the psychic-poker prompt-boundary audit (POKER_SOCIAL_SHADOW, PokerPromptEnvelope v0.7.38), the FlyLo/Grok assistant and legal-effect model, and the Observation/Virtual-Browser fail-closed contracts.
invariants: Nothing in this sphere is included 'because an LLM might be confused'. Each entry cites the real boundary contract or incident it comes from.
Detectable with a reliable mechanical trigger -> rule. Requires judging intent or trusting the boundary contract -> article.
Containment and correctness are the same discipline: a helper that over-claims is neither honest nor correct.
